sampling_model.design: \(K\) independent randomized encouragement trials, source block \(s\) containing \(n_s\) i.i.d. observations, with externally fixed target composition.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary encouragement has known \(e_s(x)\); receipt and outcome satisfy consistency, exclusion, and monotonicity.
sampling_model.overlap: \(0<p_0\le1\), \(p_s(x)\ge p_0\) on \(\mathcal H_s\), randomized-arm overlap holds, and \(\operatorname{supp}(p_T)\subseteq\bigcup_s\mathcal H_s\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-cell frequencies, arm means, and scalar residual variances are estimated empirically with deterministic floors and bounded fallbacks, making the scalar profile a total data map even at covariance boundaries. The full outcome-receipt covariance defines the population vector benchmark, but the original class does not bound its smallest eigenvalue; an ordinary plug-in inverse is therefore not the certified uniform procedure.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 identifies target potential-outcome means under conditions A1--A5; Theorem 2 uses weaker collection-level positivity; Theorem 3 uses cell-specific trial subsets and union support; and Theorem 4 identifies an average treatment effect under exchangeability in effect measure.
Equation (4) identifies a single-source transported CACE whose denominator is the instrument-to-receipt contrast in the target site, and Result 3 gives its efficient influence curve.
Theorem 3.2 establishes uniformly correct asymptotic size for an orthogonalized Anderson--Rubin LATE test.
Lemma 2 derives the efficient influence function and optimal source weights for a regular multi-source target average treatment effect.
The paper constructs weak-IV-robust inverted confidence sets and analyzes expected arc length in an invariant circular model.
Theorems 1--3 use ordered moduli to bound and construct honest confidence intervals for linear functionals over nested classes.
The paper identifies and regularly estimates a target-population CACE from a single study.

body.tldr: Separate transport of the cellwise outcome and receipt contrasts yields a computable two-coordinate program \(V_{\mathrm{vec}}\), and \(V_{\mathrm{vec}}\le V_{\mathrm{coll}}\) with strict inequality possible when several trials cover a cell. The fully empirical scalar-profiled Anderson--Rubin inversion remains uniformly honest under the original boundary-safe class. An all-procedure least-favorable family has \(V_{\mathrm{vec}}=V_{\mathrm{coll}}\) and gives the rate \(\min\{1,T_{\mathrm{coll}}^{-1/2}\}\) whenever the bounded-outcome variance constant is interior. The unconditional lower constant is multiplied by \(\beta_0=\sqrt{1-4e_0(1-e_0)v_0}\); at \(\beta_0=0\), every identified outcome ITT is zero and the minimax length is exactly zero. The lower witness can retain collection-only split support, and \(K=1\) recovers the scalar single-source result.

project_justification.gap: Dahabreh et al. establish collection and union-support identification, while weak-IV work supplies robust inversion principles. Neither literature gives all-procedure confidence-length theory for a transported noncompliance ratio, derives the vector information program created by separately transporting outcome and receipt contrasts, or characterizes the bounded-outcome boundary where the causal target collapses.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a same-class weak-ratio inference bracket that distinguishes unrestricted componentwise-transport information from a boundary-safe scalar-score procedure and remains honest under collection-only support.
project_justification.fill: The note derives the vector quadratic program and its exact relation to the scalar residual program, proves why ordinary empirical vector inverses are not uniformly data-total on the original class, establishes the scalar-profile upper bound, and constructs an all-procedure continuum on which the two programs coincide. The result is rate-sharp in the interior and has an explicit vanishing boundary factor with an exact zero-length edge case.

body.related_work: Dahabreh et al. (2023), especially Section 3.4.2 and Theorem 3, provide the collection-specific covering-set and union-support workflow used here, but do not study a noncompliance ratio or weak-identification length. Rudolph and van der Laan (2017), equation (4) and Result 3, identify and efficiently estimate a single-source transported CACE in the five-site Moving to Opportunity analysis; their target-site receipt data differ from the collection-wide receipt-contrast transport restriction used here. Su et al. (2024), Lemma 2, optimize source weights for a regular nonratio target and motivates retaining the full outcome-receipt covariance. Ma (2026), Algorithm 2.1 and Theorem 3.2, supplies an orthogonal Anderson--Rubin principle for LATE, while Mikusheva (2010) gives weak-IV robust-inversion precedent and Cai and Low (2004) give general expected-length modulus tools. None of these sources proves the present all-procedure collection-only continuum, the vector-versus-scalar comparison, or the maximal-variance boundary collapse.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The target composition \(p_T\) is externally fixed, and the finite-cell analysis excludes high-dimensional nuisance learning. The vector program is a population regular-information benchmark; attaining it uniformly would require a boundary-safe generalized-inverse or ridge analysis with an error term not controlled by the present residual-direction variance condition. The current theorem therefore certifies the scalar-profile upper bound and an all-procedure worst-case lower bound, not pointwise vector efficiency for \(K\ge2\).
body.honest_scope: Identification and the scalar-profiled coverage and length results are retained. The scalar collection program is exact only within scalar residual-score representations; the separately transported outcome and receipt contrasts generate the unrestricted vector program \(V_{\mathrm{vec}}\le V_{\mathrm{coll}}\). The minimax lower bound is all-procedure because its explicit continuum lies in the original base class and satisfies equality of these programs; it does not extend a scalar least-favorable geometry to every allocation face. For \(0<v_0<\{4e_0(1-e_0)\}^{-1}\), the upper and lower exponents match uniformly through weak compliance and collection-only overlap. At equality, boundedness forces the causal target to zero and the minimax length is zero. The exact confidence-length constant and a uniformly regularized vector-profile frontier remain outside the proved scope.
body.interpretation: The scalar strength index is a conservative uniform-inference design index, not a pointwise unrestricted efficiency bound. Separate outcome and receipt transport can make the vector program smaller at a favorable law, but the minimax supremum contains source-compatible laws on which vector and scalar programs agree. Hence no procedure can uniformly improve the scalar-profile rate over the declared strength class. The factor \(\beta_0\) records literal room to perturb a bounded outcome distribution: it is positive in every interior class and vanishes exactly when the outcome arm variances are forced to their maximum and all transported outcome ITTs equal zero.
